Hi Bethany,

Thanks again for taking time today — great to learn more about Acme Health's roadmap for patient-facing summarization and triage. Quick recap + two asks so procurement can move this toward a private offer: 

Recap from call:
- Primary workload: anonymized patient notes + chat summarization for triage (mostly short to medium sequences, 64-512 tokens).
- Expected traffic: pilot ≈ 25M tokens/month, production target 300–500M tokens/month across EU/US regions by Q1.
- Reliability/latency SLOs: sub-300ms p95 for shortest paths; fallback model acceptable during peak.

Asks for pricing / PO mapping: 
1) Confirm target $/1M tokens you want us to map into the AWS private offer (ballpark is fine). For internal planning, do you want the PO to show a single unit price for 1M tokens or tiered pricing by usage band?
2) Confirm whether procurement prefers the private offer on AWS only or if they want parallel offers on GCP/Azure marketplaces.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I will prepare a draft PO mapping to the AWS Private Offers flow with a single effective unit price and share a short cost model.
- If procurement wants tiered bands, we can surface 0–1M, 1–10M, >10M monthly bands.

If you can reply with a target $/1M tokens (range is fine) and whether AWS-only is OK, I’ll push the draft PO and cost model to you and your procurement contact.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks for the recap. Short answers below and a few clarifying notes for procurement.

1) Budget target: For pilot we’re targeting ~$800 / 1M tokens (we know this sounds high — pilot SLA + PHI-safe handling). If pilot looks good and costs drop with scale, procurement has flexibility down to ~$350–$450 / 1M for production.
2) Marketplace preference: procurement prefers an AWS Private Offer initially (we run majority of infra on AWS). If you can provide a mapped GCP/Azure PO later that’s helpful but not required now.

Procurement note (procurement@acmehealth.com): they require the PO to have a clear per-unit mapping and a line-item showing any committed monthly tokens tied to discount bands. Also need expected billing cadence (monthly).

For volumes: pilot 25M/mo starting Sept, target ramp to 400M/mo within 6–9 months. Sequence length distribution skewed short (chat) but with bursts of longer summaries.

Happy to review a draft PO — can you include an example calculation showing how the unit price translates to monthly spend at 25M and 400M tokens?

Best,
Bethany

--

Head of Product, Acme Health

Thanks Bethany — very helpful. I’ve attached a quick cost model and an initial PO mapping that shows both a single effective unit price and a tiered-band example so procurement can choose. Highlights below: 

- Option A (single effective unit price): $700 / 1M tokens — simple, easy to bill; pilot spend at 25M = $17,500/month. Production at 400M = $280,000/month.
- Option B (tiered bands): 0–50M = $800, 50–200M = $500, >200M = $350 / 1M. That produces pilot ≈ $20k and production ≈ $170k (assuming ramp into higher bands).

Notes on assumptions in the cost model (attached): we include estimated tokenization overhead, inter-region egress (if applicable), and a small margin for reserved capacity (if they want an SLA). Let me know if any of these assumptions are off and I’ll update.

Next steps:
- Bethany / procurement: if AWS-only is acceptable, confirm and I’ll initiate Private Offer preparation in the AWS Partner Console and share the PO draft (PDF) for signature.
- Internal: Jonas — can you review the attached mapping and confirm we can support the banded unit prices operationally (KV-cache, batching assumptions)? I’m also sending this to Ava for econ sanity-check.

Attaching: cost-model-v1.csv, aws-po-mapping-draft.pdf

Thanks — Hannah

--
